The bithermal fatigue lives of bare Rene N4 specimens were shorter than isothermal fatigue lives at either 760°C or 982°C when compared on an inelastic strain basis.
Both in-phase and out-of-phase bithermal fatigue life curves converged in the large strain regime and diverged in the small strain regime, with out-of-phase resulting in the shortest lives.
For isothermal fatigue at 760°C, the coated Rene N4 specimens had about an order of magnitude shorter life than the bare specimens at a similar strain range.
Crack initiation in the coated specimens occurred at the coating surface for fatigue at 760°C, while in the bare specimens it occurred at internal and surface micropores.
At 982°C, crack initiation shifted from surface oxide cracks in the bare specimens to internal pores in the coated specimens.
The coating had no effect on fatigue life for in-phase bithermal cycling, but was detrimental for out-of-phase bithermal fatigue under large strains.
Surface cracks in the bare specimens cycled in-phase were blunted by oxide spallation, while surface cracks in the out-of-phase tests were not blunted and could continue to grow into the substrate.
The Rene N4 single crystal exhibited significant porosity, about 0.4 vol%.
The coating system studied was a diffusion aluminide coating, Codep B-1, applied by pack cementation with a thickness of about 0.055 mm.
The temperature extremes of the bithermal cycle were 760°C and 982°C, with a frequency of 0.1 Hz and an R ratio of -1.
Isothermal fatigue tests were also performed at 760°C and 982°C to compare to the bithermal results.
Crack initiation in the bare specimens fatigued at 760°C occurred in a stage I manner on (111) planes, transitioning to stage II crack growth.
For bare specimens fatigued at 982°C, crack initiation occurred at surface micropores and oxide cracks, with only stage II cracking observed.
Crack initiation in the coated specimens fatigued at 982°C occurred at internal pores, with stage II cracking dominating.
Spallation of the oxide scale was observed during long-term testing of the bare specimens.
